solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters only

blocks.note: the two end letters of love
a toff is a posh, upper-class person; the question mark admits a toff is not strictly a noble

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a love that comes free is an aristocratic thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Toff is British slang for a well-to-do, upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: To let someone off is to release them without punishment, to set them at liberty.

indicators.note: in says the letters wanted sit inside the following words, running across the comma

blocks.note: found running from the end of context into the start of remain

explanation.surface: Advice that, read in context, the furthest points stay where they are.
explanation.definitionFit: Extrema are the maximum and minimum values of a function, the outermost or extreme points of something.

blocks.note: something exposed is out in the open
zip means nothing, the figure zero
faction can mean dissension or discord within a group

explanation.surface: A garment's bust is on show because the zip has failed.
explanation.walkthrough: Bust looks like part of a dress, but it is the definition: broken. Zip, which seems to be the fastener, gives a zero.
explanation.definitionFit: A bust machine is broken and no longer working, which is what being disabled from working means.

blocks.note: f is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references
a defeat is a loss

explanation.surface: Feeling a bit low after losing a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Down here is soft fluffy material, not low spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Floss is the soft silky fibre from certain plants or cocoons, a fluffy material like the plumage down.

blocks.note: A is the usual abbreviation for answer
taken as written
answer with a D tacked on spells answered, whose synonym is solved

explanation.surface: Reads like a quiz instruction: give answer B and answer D for question 1.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the cross-reference: 1 is the answer to 1 across, LET OFF. The joke is that answer plus D makes answered, so A + B + SOLVED gives ABSOLVED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be let off a charge or sin is to be pardoned or freed from blame, cleared entirely.

clue.text: Some joiners saw this as out of character

definitions.text: Some joiners saw this as out of character

blocks.clueFragment: Some joiners saw this as out of character
blocks.note: surface reading: some people who join a club see a certain behaviour as untypical
setter's reading: carpenters cut wood across its fibres, and the same phrase means contrary to one's nature

explanation.surface: Some members of a group consider a piece of behaviour uncharacteristic.
explanation.walkthrough: Joiners are woodworkers and saw is their verb, not 'perceive'; sawing across the fibres of timber is the literal image behind the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes doing something contrary to one's natural inclination, as cutting wood across its fibres goes contrary to it.

clue.text: Cut across area that’s fine but not in shelter

indicators.note: but not in tells us to take a word and remove a pair of letters spelling the little word in
across means one piece stretches over and around the others, holding them inside

blocks.note: shaven means cut close, as a beard is
A is the abbreviation for area
fine with its in removed

explanation.surface: A shortcut across a spot that seems all right, yet offers no shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: Cut looks like a verb or a noun, but here it is the adjective shaven, which is split open to hold the other letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A safe haven is a place of refuge or protection, which is just what a shelter provides.

indicators.note: over in a down clue means turned over, so the letters run backwards up the column

blocks.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A garland remains, left over from some celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is a Hawaiian wreath of flowers worn around the neck, a type of flower necklace.

indicators.note: One in Ten says one thing is placed inside the other

blocks.note: EPs are extended-play records
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A band's manager puts out a record called One in Ten.
explanation.walkthrough: One in Ten was a UB40 single, making the surface plausible. Brian Epstein managed the Beatles.
explanation.definitionFit: Brian Epstein was the manager who guided the Beatles to fame in the early 1960s.

blocks.note: to declare something is to state it
love is zero in tennis, a nought
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
affairs are romances; the apostrophe is read as making a plural

explanation.surface: Confessing love, the fine romance is in a certain state.
explanation.walkthrough: A Fine Romance is a classic song, which disguises fine as a mere adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of affairs is the way things stand at a given moment, the situation or circumstances.

clue.text: Will the author matter on reflection? Almost

definitions.note: the novelist Will Self; the definition gives his surname

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is cut off
a reflection in a mirror shows things the wrong way round, so read the letters backwards

blocks.note: flesh is physical matter, the body as opposed to the spirit

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a writer will be important once people think it over.
explanation.walkthrough: Will reads as the verb opening a question, but it is the first name of the British novelist Will Self.
explanation.definitionFit: Will Self is a British novelist and journalist, so his surname is what the author's name leads to.

indicators.note: to skirt something is to go round its edge, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: a grass is an informer, one who shops others to the police
with and and both mean together with

explanation.surface: Grass skirts paired with a woolly jumper: an odd outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass and shop are British slang for informing on someone. A jumper is a sweater in Britain, but here it means a creature that leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: The sandhopper is a small beach crustacean famous for leaping about, so it is literally a jumper.

blocks.note: first meaning: rash and hasty, rushing ahead
second meaning: to come down as rain or snow, or settle out of a solution

explanation.surface: A headfirst tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for hasty, rash action and a verb for moisture coming down from clouds or solids settling.

clue.text: Lawyers accepting account at card game

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: the Bar is the collective name for barristers
acc. is an abbreviation for account
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lawyers playing cards on account at a casino.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccarat is a casino gambling game played with cards, in which players bet on hands.

indicators.note: something criminal is wrong or crooked, so the letters are bent out of order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A criminal in Britain releases a political dissident.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusenik was a Soviet Jew refused permission to emigrate, and more broadly anyone who refuses to comply in protest.

clue.text: Victor and Annie cooking a sort of sausage

indicators.note: cooking means preparing or mixing up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: Victor is V in the radio alphabet
the letters of Annie rearranged

explanation.surface: Two people, Victor and Annie, frying up a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: A Vienna sausage is a thin smoked frankfurter-style sausage, so Vienna names a type of sausage.

indicators.note: oddly means keep only the letters in odd positions: first, third and so on

blocks.note: first and third letters of that
a jam session is musicians improvising, and a riff is a repeated improvised phrase

explanation.surface: Asking whether a menu, strangely, offers jam.
explanation.walkthrough: Jam sits naturally on a menu as food; the question mark flags the musical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a list of charges, as in a hotel or restaurant price list or bill of fare.

indicators.note: across means stretched over and around, so one piece contains the other

blocks.note: to charge someone with a crime is to accuse them
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone charging across a river and swearing in frustration.
explanation.definitionFit: To accurse is the archaic verb meaning to place a curse upon, to condemn or call down evil on.

clue.text: Party for Her Highness interrupted by news

indicators.note: something interrupted is broken into, so another piece goes in the middle

blocks.note: highness is the state of being high, i.e. height
N stands for new, and the plural gives two Ns

explanation.surface: A celebration for a royal lady is disrupted by a news report.
explanation.walkthrough: Her Highness looks like a royal title, but the words split: Her belongs to the definition. A hen night is a British bride-to-be's party with her female friends.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen night is a celebration held for a woman before her wedding, so it is her party.

clue.text: Battle-axe that man will throw up

blocks.note: he'll is short for he will
to cat is British slang for to vomit

explanation.surface: A fierce woman whom a man is going to vomit over.
explanation.walkthrough: Battle-axe is not a weapon here but a domineering woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A hellcat is a fierce, spiteful or bad-tempered woman, much like a formidable battle-axe.

clue.text: One gun’s shot in smoke, producing white powder

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so the letters are knocked out of order
in says the mixed letters go inside the following word

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a cigar is something to smoke
the letters of guns rearranged

explanation.surface: A gunshot in the smoke leaves white powder, like a crime scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The powder suggests gunpowder or drugs, but it is the baker's sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing sugar is very finely ground sugar used for cake icing, a fine white powder.

clue.text: Lunatic tries to take exam again

indicators.note: lunatic means crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A mad student attempts to sit an exam a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To resit is the British term for sitting an examination again after failing it.

clue.text: Not working, taking some paid leave

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: found running from the end of paid into the start of leave

explanation.surface: Off work, using some of one's holiday entitlement.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone idle is inactive or unoccupied, doing nothing and so not at work.

indicators.note: something blocked by another has that other wedged inside it

blocks.note: a renaissance is a rebirth or revival
a con is a swindle or fraud

explanation.surface: The revival of the Scout movement is thwarted by a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: Reconnaissance is military surveying of enemy ground, gathering information as scouts do.

indicators.note: sound means we want a word as it is heard when spoken, not as it is written

blocks.note: the core is the heart of something

explanation.surface: Listening to one's own heartbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: My is an exclamation of surprise, not a possessive. Cor is a British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Cor is a British exclamation of astonishment, much like saying my or gosh.

blocks.note: to carry is to bear
one's own people are one's family

explanation.surface: Someone carries a hat of their own.
explanation.walkthrough: A bearskin is the tall black fur cap worn by British guardsmen, for instance outside Buckingham Palace.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearskin is a tall fur headdress worn ceremonially by guards regiments, a kind of military cap.

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: an experiment is a try or attempt
to put away food is to eat it

explanation.surface: A formal agreement filed away during a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between states, a binding compact or pact.
